categories.name: Direct Payment
categories.description: Fines that are paid quickly after creation or fine notification with minimal steps and no escalation or penalties.
categories.rationale: High frequency variants representing straightforward, low-duration payment paths.

categories.name: Standard Collection
categories.description: Fines that undergo standard notification, penalty addition, and eventually progress to credit collection due to non-payment.
categories.rationale: Represents the most common long-duration resolution path ending in credit collection.

categories.name: Delayed Payment with Penalties
categories.description: Fines where penalties are added and notifications sent, but the offender eventually makes a payment after a moderate delay, sometimes involving multiple payment installments.
categories.rationale: Captures recurring patterns of late payments accompanied by penalty increments and repeated payment actions.

categories.name: Prefecture Appeal Path
categories.description: Processes that involve submitting an appeal to the prefecture, receiving results, and handling notifications or subsequent legal/collection steps.
categories.rationale: Groups variants characterized by formal appeals to the prefecture and associated administrative handling.

categories.name: Chronic Installment Rework
categories.description: Extremely long traces characterized by a high frequency of repeated payment steps spanning multiple months or years.
categories.rationale: Identifies extreme outliers with unusually high trace lengths driven by repetitive payment installments.
